scope: source-only; owner screenshot not seen, no screenshot retrieval attempted; Mac owns runtime RCA

diagnosticDefinitions.visibility: alpha>=128 unless alpha-weighted metric explicitly named
diagnosticDefinitions.luma: Yprime=.2126R+.7152G+.0722B on sRGB8 code values, not linear-light physical luminance
diagnosticDefinitions.pale: visible && Yprime>=170 && minRGB>=140 && (maxRGB-minRGB)<=60; heuristic neutral/pale-feather pixel selection, not semantic whiteness or an art gate
diagnosticDefinitions.connectivity: 8-connected components; tiny means1or2pixels at the reported resolution
diagnosticDefinitions.interior: visible mask eroded by one3x3pixel step at that resolution; pixel-size dependent, not a matched anatomical region
diagnosticDefinitions.commonWorldSize: 96→64 nearest-only at density1.5; no per-bird fit. Canon published density differs and is also shown separately.
diagnosticDefinitions.componentInterpretation: Native/output/world component counts are not directly scale invariant. Tiny-component statistics diagnose sampling/texture, not defects or screenshot causality.

finding: No color-darkening transform found in these retained Anna source/export paths. All five exported RGBA arrays exactly equal the selected native1024 source pixels; small global visible-luma mean changes are nearest-sampling population changes. This does not diagnose the unavailable owner screenshot or current Mac rendering.
nativeLineageCheck: At alpha>=128, every registered visible pixel in all five frames also exactly maps back to its original generated atlas at the documented crop/translation. No visible RGB/alpha change was detected in native-atlas→registered-source or registered-source→96 export.
manualVisualFindings: The generated native canon and action sources already contain high-frequency pale gray/white breast feather flecks, olive/green highlights and brown/dark folded-wing feather lines. These details were not invented by the96 export.

Rose crown/throat, green upperparts and long thin dark bill remain recognizable in the source family. New perched poses remain about32.67world units wide under their declared density, compared with34 for the first canon under its different density.
At a common density1.5, the old canon becomes29.33world units wide while new perched poses remain32.67. Forcing every body to34 would be a different fit and was deliberately not performed.

At common64canvas nearest presentation the bird is tiny and high-frequency plumage is represented by a small set of contrasting pixels. Pale speck components are present, but component counts are not a semantic defect criterion.

No owner screenshot pixels, brown feeder bird, corvid comparison, real feeder overlap, runtime tint or current Mac rendering was inspected in this audit. Parent descriptions are context, not source-pixel evidence.

establishedLocally: Native source feather texture includes pale/interior color variation.
All visible atlas→registered pixel mappings tested are byte-exact.
All five1024→96 nearest outputs are byte-exact at the selected coordinates.
Per-frame whole-visible luma means change by sampling only; the new perched exports are slightly brighter by this metric, not darker.
Published old and new Anna presentation densities differ.
possibleButUnproven: Fine source texture may appear noisy at tiny presentation sizes.
Different presentation density/device scaling and background contrast may alter perceived detail/brightness.
Mac opacity, tint, filter, blending, color-space or premultiplied-alpha handling could change actual rendering; these were not tested.
Overlapping birds/feeder geometry or mismatched contact placement could create a visual mixture.
Fast alternating wing area could create temporal contrast/strobing distinct from a per-pixel color transform.
notEstablished: That the unavailable screenshot depicts Anna.
That these source textures caused the owner's reported brown-bird mottling/darkness.
That the current Mac renderer darkens these assets.
That exporting a different palette or regenerating art would fix the reported issue.
